newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WA NEWS SAID TRADING FLAT SINCE YR-END.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WA NEWS SAID TRADING FLAT SINCE YR-END.

text.p: West Australian Newspapers Holdings Ltd said on Thursday that trading conditions have remained flat since its financial year ended on June 30.

The group earlier reported a net profit of A$49.43 million for the year ended June 30, up 3.3 percent over 1995/96 which contained one extra week. Total revenue edged for the year up 0.2 percent to A$298.26 million.

WA Newspapers said trading conditions in the fourth quarter improved marginally. However, the main classified segments of real estate and employment continued to languish, restrained by lack of consumer confidence, it said.
WA Newspapers said net advertising revenue of the West Australian newspaper fell by 0.4 percent to A$179.65 million and net circulation revenue rose by 0.5 percent to A$53.86 million.
Advertising volumes fell 8.3 percent, with display down by 8.9 percent, classifieds down by 7.8 percent and new homes down by 9.5 percent, the company said.
Total operating costs eased by 0.3 percent to A$155.87 million while newsprint costs fell by 5.5 percent to A$50.72 million.
WA Newspapers said its result was after an abnormal loss of A$0.96 million relating to redundancy and retraining costs.
Operating profit before abnormals and tax rose 5.1 percent to A$78.71 million, it said.
The group held its year dividend at 25 cents fully franked.

The company said it had adopted equity accounting of its interest in Comunity Newspapers Group Ltd in the year but the effect was minimal because previously, Community Newspapers had distributed 100 percent of after-tax profits as dividend to its parent.
